rubric_artifacts.behaviour: the downside anchor lands within 1% of the close (QCOM's 200-day is 0.54% below the close; RKT's low target of $14.00 is 0.4% below the $14.06 close), so the computed risk-to-reward is 26.8:1 and 60.7:1. These numbers are arithmetic, not analysis, and neither was allowed to drive a verdict. A future rubric should reject an anchor closer than about 5% to the close and fall back to the next one down.

the gate requires the guide to be held or raised, so a company that gives no guidance can never pass it however good the print. PLPC beat by 86% on EPS and rose 30% on the day and still fails. Noted; it did not change either name's tier, since both fail a second gate.
